summary:
The Meskwaki name means Red Earth People. The Meskwaki are an Algonquian people of the Eastern Woodlands. Their oral tradition places their beginnings far to the east. Over generations they moved west through the Great Lakes country to the lands that became Wisconsin, Illinois and Iowa. The French called them Renards, or Foxes, which is where the English name "Fox" comes from.

In the early 1700s the Meskwaki fought years of war against the French and their Native allies, and they lost many people. During that century they allied with the Sauk, a closely related people with a similar language. That alliance, and an 1804 treaty that treated the two as one tribe, gave rise to the federal name "Sac and Fox." The Meskwaki have always been their own people.

In the 1840s, treaties signed under that combined name took the Meskwaki's Iowa lands and sent them to Kansas. Many refused to go, and others came home. In 1857 they bought land of their own in Tama County, Iowa. That purchase grew into the Meskwaki Settlement, which is home today to the Meskwaki Nation, federally known as the Sac and Fox Tribe of the Mississippi in Iowa. The Nation runs its own school and works to keep the Meskwaki language and culture strong.

notes: Word count is about 220. 'Red Earth People' is backed by Iowa PBS, OHS and NPS. 'Renards' and 'always Meskwaki' come from meskwaki.org. The eastern origin and westward migration come from Iowa PBS (oral tradition), with NPS adding Michigan and Wisconsin. The French wars are backed by Iowa PBS and by the Missouri nation's reference to a French attack on the Foxes. The 1857 purchase is backed by meskwaki.org, SHSI and Iowa PBS. LEFT OUT: (1) The Fox Wars dates (1701–1716 and 1733). Only Iowa PBS gives them. (2) Lake Saint-Jean, Quebec, as the origin place in oral tradition. Only Iowa PBS gives it, and it was kept general on purpose. (3) Population-collapse figures. (4) The 1842 treaty by name and year. Only Iowa PBS gives them. (5) The 1856 Iowa law, to stay within length. It has three sources and could be added back.
